integrity: The arbitrary-graph theorem is proved analytically by support functions, central symmetry, a finite layer-cake identity, discrete coarea, and equality on centered cut indicators. The finite enumeration is corroborative only and is not used as an infinite proof.
scientific_limitations: The result assumes a connected finite simple graph with positive edge weights and uses the intrinsic standard Euclidean metric in the affine hull. It does not classify all Chebyshev centers, disconnected cases, other norms, circumradii, or John ellipsoids. A residual originality risk is that the equivalent finite-graph L1-gradient/L2-function quotient may occur under different Sobolev terminology, although no graphical-zonotope inradius identification was found in the inspected literature.
title: Euclidean inradius of weighted graphical zonotopes is a cut expansion constant
